issue.explanation: Consider using `apply()` instead of `commit` on shared preferences. Whereas `commit` blocks and writes its data to persistent storage immediately, `apply` will handle it in the background.

issue.message: Use of `REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS` violates the Play Store Content Policy regarding acceptable use cases, as described in https://developer.android.com/training/monitoring-device-state/doze-standby.html
issue.explanation:
This issue flags code that either * negatively affects battery life, or * uses APIs that have recently changed behavior to prevent background tasks from consuming memory and battery excessively.
Generally, you should be using `WorkManager` instead.
For more details on how to update your code, please see https://developer.android.com/topic/performance/background-optimization

issue.message: Missing x86_64 ABI support for ChromeOS
issue.explanation: To properly support ChromeOS, your Android application should have an x86 and/or x86_64 binary as part of the build configuration. To fix the issue, ensure your files are properly optimized for ARM; the binary translator will then ensure compatibility with x86. Alternatively, add an `abiSplit` for x86 within your `build.gradle` file and create the required x86 dependencies.
issue.errorLine1: debug { signingConfig = null; ndk { abiFilters += listOf("arm64-v8a", "armeabi-v7a") } }

issue.message: Do not place Android context classes in static fields (static reference to `TimingTrace` which has field `context` pointing to `Context`); this is a memory leak
issue.explanation:
A static field will leak contexts.
Non-static inner classes have an implicit reference to their outer class. If that outer class is for example a `Fragment` or `Activity`, then this reference means that the long-running handler/loader/task will hold a reference to the activity which prevents it from getting garbage collected.
Similarly, direct field references to activities and fragments from these longer running instances can cause leaks.
ViewModel classes should never point to Views or non-application Contexts.

issue.message: Should explicitly set `android:icon`, there is no default
issue.explanation: You should set an icon for the application as whole because there is no default. This attribute must be set as a reference to a drawable resource containing the image (for example `@drawable/icon`).
